Subject: Clarification: directory-sync authority, SCIM role bindings (RFP §4.2)

Alex / Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP response so far — Dirigo procurement and InfoSec reviewed section 4.2 (Identity & Access) and had a few clarifying questions before we move to the final technical sync. Can you confirm the following points?

1) SCIM provisioning: can Redwood act as a SCIM "service provider" for Dirigo's IdP such that we can provision users and groups from Azure AD? Specifically we need to know whether Redwood supports: PATCH operations, incremental delta syncs, bulk replace, and an option to provision group -> role mappings (e.g., map AAD group X -> Redwood role "Model Admin").

2) Delegated admin via SCIM: is there a way to create scoped admin roles via SCIM (org-wide vs project-scoped)? Dirigo needs the ability to grant narrow admin rights to our platform owners.

3) SAML/OIDC: does Redwood accept AAD and Google Workspace assertions with group claims? We need a short list of required/optional claim names and any special transformation rules.

4) Deprovisioning SLA: in the event of a user removal/disable in AD, how long until token/session revocation occurs on Redwood? We have a security requirement for emergency deprovisioning.

5) Audit evidence: can you provide sample admin/audit logs showing role changes and SCIM events, and indicate retention period?

Attached: Dirigo_RFP_v3.pdf with highlighted questions. Please let me know if you prefer a 30-minute technical call — we're aiming to close questions by EOD 2028-01-15.

Regards,
Samantha Ortiz
Senior IT Sourcing
Dirigo Systems

Team — draft technical answer below (feel free to edit for tone). I'll attach a sample SCIM mapping CSV and a redacted audit excerpt.

SCIM provisioning (short):
- Supported operations: CREATE/GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. PATCH uses RFC7644 JSON Patch semantics; we also support bulk replace via a bulk endpoint (/scim/v2/Bulk).
- Delta/incremental sync: we provide change tokens and the /scim/v2/Users?filter=meta.lastModified gt "<timestamp>" pattern. For Azure AD provisioning, outbound provisioning uses incremental PATCHs; full replace is supported for initial syncs.
- Attribute names: we accept standard SCIM attributes: userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work].value, externalId, active. Groups are represented via /scim/v2/Groups with members referencing user id.
- Group -> role mapping: we support a configurable mapping table (managed in Console or via Admin API) where an external group identifier maps to one or more Redwood roles. This mapping can be set via SCIM extension attributes or via a one-time import. The mapping table is exportable as CSV (/api/v1/admin/scim-mappings).

Delegated admin & scoping:
- Role model: default roles include Organization Admin, Billing Admin, Project Admin, Model Admin, Viewer.
- Scoping: roles may be scoped to the organization or to specific projects/environments. Project-level scoping is expressed as an explicit attribute (scope:project:<project_id>) on the role binding.
- SCIM settable fields: role bindings can be created through SCIM by writing a RoleBinding resource extension (urn:redwood:scim:RoleBinding) on the User resource. Example: { "urn:redwood:scim:RoleBinding": [{"role":"Project Admin","scope":"project:proj-123"}] }.

SAML/OIDC support:
- SAML: support for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, metadata upload, multiple ACS endpoints, and group assertions via SAML attribute (name=Groups or custom claim). We accept group claims either as a semicolon-comma separated list or as SAML 2.0 Attribute values. Required attributes: Subject (NameID or eduPersonPrincipalName), email, displayName (recommended).
- OIDC: we accept standard id_token claims (sub, email, name) and optional groups claim. For Okta/Azure AD we recommend sending groups in the groups claim or via the group membership API + SCIM for provisioning.

Deprovisioning SLA (practical details):
- SCIM deprovisioning (DELETE/active=false): typical processing latency is sub-60s for single user operations under normal load; however, we recommend a conservative contractual SLA of 5 minutes for acknowledgement and 15 minutes for propagation in multi-region deployments.
- Session/token revocation: access tokens issued by Redwood are short-lived (default 15 minutes) and refresh tokens can be revoked immediately upon SCIM remove event; gateways will reject new requests after token invalidation. For emergency deprovisioning we provide an admin API to revoke sessions instantly.

Audit logs and retention:
- Audit events for SCIM operations and role changes are logged as structured events; sample fields: timestamp, actor_id, event_type, target_resource, diff.
- Retention: 13 months by default for audit events, exportable via API and available in Console. We can offer extended retention as an add-on.

Attachments I will produce: redwood_scim_mapping.csv (sample group->role mappings) and a redacted audit CSV (events_deid.csv). Also propose short SLA language.
